title: Distinguish demo, Lab, sandbox and pilot
nav: 2. Distinguish demo, Lab, sandbox and pilot
objective: Which facts must be rechecked before offering a customer a sandbox?.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: The validation options differ in what data they use, how faithfully they reflect permissions, who can use them, and what their results can prove. Know the differences, and check the current details before you offer one.

blocks.x: Before offering an option, write down its current, approved description: data type, permission fidelity, allowed users, duration, setup owner, security, cost, and what the result can prove. Environment details change between versions of Glean's guides. For example, sandbox access, data options, and limits have been described differently over time. Flag any differences you find.

blocks.label: Boundary
blocks.x: Don't teach dated pricing, revenue thresholds, shared-login behavior, or environment limits as permanent facts. Confirm the live terms with the Glean account team before offering an option to a customer.

Teams use these names inconsistently, so confirm what each person means. In Glean's validation-events training, "Glean Lab" is described as another name for the sandbox option, and "POC" is often used for a pilot, though a proof of concept can also be a sandbox. The same training notes that a customer can separately purchase a sandbox instance after becoming a customer, which is different from a sandbox used for validation.

The training also clarifies the data behind the lighter options. A custom demo late in the sale often uses customer files that have been uploaded, and the sandbox uses uploaded files too. In both cases, no connectors are set up. A pilot is the first option that connects to the customer's systems.

blocks.title: What each validation option uses
blocks.alt: A comparison of validation options and the data each uses. A tailored demo uses a prepared scenario or uploaded customer files, with no connectors. A sandbox uses uploaded files for an allotted group of users, with no connectors. A pilot connects to the customer's systems for a defined cohort.
